name: Absci
description: Generative AI drug creation company pairing zero-shot antibody design with high-throughput wet-lab validation for better biologics.
longDescription: Absci's Integrated Drug Creation platform couples deep-learning antibody design with rapid experimental screening. It claims zero-shot generative design and validation of new antibodies, with partners across pharma for AI-designed biologics. Novel targets are discovered via reverse immunology from super immune responders.

name: Agent Laboratory
description: End-to-end autonomous research workflow where LLM agents do literature review, experimentation, and report writing to produce complete papers.
longDescription: Agent Laboratory (arXiv 2501.04227, Johns Hopkins/AMD) is an end-to-end autonomous research workflow that takes a research idea and produces code, experiments, and a full research report. It uses specialized agents such as a PhD agent and postdoc agent across three phases: literature review, experimentation, and report writing. It is a general AI-research foundation that bio groups adapt for their own pipelines.

name: AI for Medicine Specialization
description: DeepLearning.AI specialization applying deep learning to medical diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment through hands-on programming assignments.
longDescription: This DeepLearning.AI specialization on Coursera teaches practical machine learning for medicine: medical diagnosis from imaging, prognosis estimation, and treatment effect estimation. Courses include AI for Medical Diagnosis, AI for Medical Prognosis, and AI for Medical Treatment, with hands-on labs. It is the most accessible structured entry point for ML engineers moving into medical AI.

name: AIAgents4Pharma
description: Open-source suite of AI agents that help pharma researchers query and reason over biomedical data across drug discovery workflows.
longDescription: AIAgents4Pharma (Team VPE, Virtual Patient Engine) is an open-source project bringing together AI agents that let researchers and pharma companies interact with complex biomedical data. It packages LLM-driven agents and tools spanning literature, chemistry, and omics for end-to-end drug discovery support. It is one of the most complete dedicated open-source agent frameworks for pharma workflows.

name: AlphaFold 2
description: Official open-source implementation of AlphaFold 2, the breakthrough system that predicted protein structures with near-experimental accuracy.
longDescription: AlphaFold 2's 2020 CASP14 result and 2021 open-source release transformed structural biology. Its code, plus nearly 200 million predictions via AlphaFold DB, underpin much of modern computational biology. The repository remains the canonical reference implementation for protein structure prediction.

name: AlphaFold 3
description: Google DeepMind's AI system predicting 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, ligands and modifications directly from sequence descriptions.
longDescription: AlphaFold 3 extends the AlphaFold lineage to nearly all biomolecular interactions, including protein-ligand and antibody-antigen complexes. DeepMind open-sourced the inference pipeline code, with trained model parameters available separately under a non-commercial license. It set the accuracy bar that open models like Boltz and Chai-1 now chase.

name: AlphaFold DB
description: Open-access database of 200M+ predicted protein structures from DeepMind and EMBL-EBI, searchable and downloadable by UniProt accession.
longDescription: AlphaFold DB makes AlphaFold predictions for nearly every cataloged protein freely available through a web interface and public FTP. It has grown to over 260 million structures and is default infrastructure for biologists needing a quick structural view. EMBL-EBI co-develops and hosts the resource with Google DeepMind.

name: AlphaFold Server
description: Free web tool from Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs predicting how proteins interact with DNA, RNA, ligands, and ions using AlphaFold 3.
longDescription: AlphaFold Server (alphafoldserver.com) provides free web access to AlphaFold 3, described by Google as the most accurate tool for predicting protein interactions with DNA, RNA, ligands, and other molecules. It extends AlphaFold 2's protein-only predictions to full biomolecular complexes through a simple form-based interface. Together with the 200M-structure AlphaFold Database it underpins much of modern AI-driven structural biology.

name: AlphaGenome
description: DeepMind's 2025 unified DNA model predicting gene expression, splicing and chromatin at near single-base resolution from 1M-base inputs.
longDescription: AlphaGenome takes DNA sequences up to one million base pairs and predicts thousands of molecular properties across 11 regulatory modalities. It targets the non-coding 'dark matter' of the genome to help interpret how mutations impact health. A Python API client and research code are available on GitHub.

name: Anthropic Agent Skills
description: Anthropic's official public repository of example Agent Skills — the reference implementation of the open SKILL.md skill format.
longDescription: anthropics/skills is the canonical public repository demonstrating Claude's skills system, from creative applications to practical document handling. The SKILL.md format it popularized is now supported by Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and community collections, making it the de facto packaging standard for agent skills. Start here to learn the format before writing or auditing bio skills.

name: Anthropic Life Sciences Marketplace
description: Official Anthropic marketplace of MCP servers and skills for life sciences tools, installable into Claude Code for research workflows.
longDescription: anthropics/life-sciences is Anthropic's Life Sciences Marketplace for Claude Code: a plugin collection of MCP servers and skills exposing specialized research tools and databases. It accompanies the Claude for Life Sciences launch, which added scientific connectors and drug-discovery-oriented capabilities. The clearest signal that life-science agent tooling is now a first-party ecosystem.

name: Artificial intelligence in drug development (review)
description: Highly cited Nature Medicine review by Zhang et al. surveying AI applications across the entire drug development workflow.
longDescription: This Nature Medicine review (s41591-024-03434-4, Zhang et al.) surveys how AI is applied across the whole drug development workflow, from target identification to clinical outcomes, and has accumulated 600+ citations. It is the standard modern reference for framing where machine learning actually adds value in pharma. A useful companion is Bajorath's editorial Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery: Into the Great Wide Open (J. Med. Chem. 2020).

name: AutoDock Vina
description: One of the fastest and most widely used open-source molecular docking engines for virtual screening and binding pose prediction.
longDescription: AutoDock Vina, designed by Oleg Trott at The Scripps Research Institute, is one of the fastest and most widely used open-source docking engines for predicting how small molecules bind to receptors. It is a turnkey computational docking program used heavily in drug discovery and virtual screening, with multi-core support and a GPU-accelerated variant (AutoDock-GPU). It remains the baseline against which newer AI docking methods are compared.

name: Awesome Bio Agent Skills
description: Curated collection of 1,676 self-contained SKILL.md biomedical agent skills, deduplicated from 20 open-source repos into 15 categories.
longDescription: BioTender-max/awesome-bio-agent-skills aggregates 1,676 SKILL.md-format agent skills for biomedical research — genomics, proteomics, single-cell analysis, clinical AI, protein design — deduplicated from 20 open-source repositories into 15 categories. Skills are compatible with OpenClaw, NanoClaw, Biomni, and other agent frameworks. The largest single shelf of ready-to-install bio skills today.

name: Awesome Bioinformatics
description: The classic curated list of bioinformatics libraries and software, organized by sequence analysis, assembly, variant calling, and more.
longDescription: danielecook/Awesome-Bioinformatics is the long-standing community awesome list for bioinformatics software, covering sequence analysis, genome assembly, variant calling, data formats, and tooling. It shows recent activity (commits as recent as April 2026) and is widely cited as the starting point for bioinformatics software discovery. Pairs well with bio.tools for structured metadata.

name: awesome-agents4science
description: Curated papers on LLMs and AI agents for scientific research and development, maintained by the OSU NLP Group.
longDescription: OSU-NLP-Group/awesome-agents4science tracks the fast-growing literature on LLM-based agents for science — autonomous experimentation, discovery, and research automation. It is the paper-level companion to tool lists when you need evidence on how agents actually perform in scientific workflows. Maintained by The Ohio State University NLP group.

name: awesome-ai-bio-labs
description: Curated, auditable directory of AI-first biology labs worldwide, organized lab-by-lab with provenance-tagged data.
longDescription: BioTender-max/awesome-ai-bio-labs is a curated directory of AI-first biology labs worldwide, organized around labs and teams with provenance-tagged entries. It is also browsable as a website at biotender.online/labs. Useful for finding who is actually building BioAI, not just which tools exist.

name: awesome-ai-for-science
description: Curated list of AI tools, libraries, papers, datasets, and frameworks accelerating scientific discovery across physics, chemistry, and biology.
longDescription: ai-boost/awesome-ai-for-science (backed by the ai4s-research org) organizes AI-for-science resources by domain — biology, chemistry, physics, and beyond — covering tools, papers, datasets, and frameworks, including agent skill packs like GDM science-skills. It has trended on TrendShift and is widely shared as a way to keep up with fast-moving AI-for-science developments. The umbrella list under which BioAI sits.

name: Awesome-AI-Meets-Biology
description: Collection of state-of-the-art and novel LLMs and agents across biomedical and bioinformatics fields.
longDescription: Webioinfo01/Awesome-AI-Meets-Biology gathers notable LLMs and agents for biomedical and bioinformatics applications. The same organization maintains spin-off lists such as Awesome-LLMs-meet-genomes and Awesome-Virtual-Cell. A compact snapshot of the BioAI model and agent landscape rather than a tools catalog.

name: awesome-AIDD
description: Popular curated list for AI-aided drug discovery covering molecular and protein representations, structure prediction, design, and enzyme engineering.
longDescription: daiyun02211/awesome-AIDD tracks AI-aided drug discovery research across molecular and protein representations, protein structure prediction, protein design, and enzyme engineering. It surfaces regularly alongside the BioAI agent directories in search results. A strong bridge between the deep-learning literature and practical molecular design tools.

name: awesome-cheminformatics
description: Curated list of cheminformatics software, resources, and libraries — mostly command-line based, free, or open-source.
longDescription: hsiaoyi0504/awesome-cheminformatics is the go-to awesome list for cheminformatics tooling: mostly CLI-based, free or open-source software for molecular handling, descriptors, and search. It is often paired with Pat Walters' opinionated open-source cheminformatics resources list. The chemistry-side companion to drug-discovery and BioAI lists.

name: awesome-deep-learning-single-cell-papers
description: Curated papers on deep learning for single-cell analysis, maintained by the OmicsML organization.
longDescription: OmicsML/awesome-deep-learning-single-cell-papers collects deep-learning papers for single-cell analysis, from classic representations to recent foundation models. The same organization maintains the companion awesome-foundation-model-single-cell-papers tracking the current wave of single-cell foundation models. The essential reading list for AI approaches to single-cell data.

name: awesome-drug-discovery
description: Meticulously curated resource list on computational drug discovery: compound databases, docking, QSAR, retrosynthesis, AI/ML frameworks, and MD.
longDescription: yboulaamane/awesome-drug-discovery focuses on computational methods for drug discovery — compound databases, docking tools, QSAR, retrosynthesis, AI/ML frameworks, and molecular dynamics. Shared and discussed on r/comp_chem, it has become the most prominent current awesome list under this name. An older repo, xnuohz/awesome-drug-discovery, archives the earlier deep-learning papers generation.

name: awesome-genomic-skills
description: Curated index of agent skills and MCP servers for genomics and bioinformatics from DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, and community projects.
longDescription: GoekeLab's awesome-genomic-skills is the map of the bio agent-skills ecosystem: skill libraries (Google DeepMind science-skills, OpenAI life-science-research, Anthropic life-sciences, AWS Kiro bundle, ClawBio, SciAgent-skills), life-science MCP servers (biomcp, gget-mcp, Seqera, plant-genomics-mcp), and agent benchmarks like BixBench and LAB-Bench. CC0-licensed and maintained by a genomics research lab, it cleanly distinguishes skills from MCP servers. The best single entry point for this whole category.

name: awesome-medical-ai-skills
description: International-edition curated list of medical and healthcare AI agent skills, MCP servers, and clinical tools.
longDescription: JuneYaooo/awesome-medical-ai-skills (International Edition) curates agent skills, MCP servers, and tools for medical and healthcare AI. It complements the same author's awesome-medical-ai list of open-source medical AI projects spanning LLMs, imaging, multi-agent systems, and clinical software. The medical counterpart to the genomics skill lists.

name: awesome-medical-imaging
description: Awesome list of software used for medical imaging research, from DICOM tooling to segmentation and analysis frameworks.
longDescription: fepegar/awesome-medical-imaging collects software for medical imaging research — formats, viewers, registration, segmentation, and analysis tooling. It is recommended in the Bioconductor community blog roundup of awesome lists and remains one of the few actively maintained entries in this niche. Pairs naturally with dataset lists like AMID for imaging AI work.

name: Awesome-Scientific-Skills
description: Open curated list of agent skills for science, including wet-lab, life-science, and bioinformatics skills.
longDescription: InternScience/Awesome-Scientific-Skills curates agent skills across scientific domains, including wet-lab protocols, life sciences, and bioinformatics. It complements GoekeLab's genomics-focused list with broader coverage of experimental science skills. Part of the fast-forming scientific skills ecosystem around SKILL.md.

name: awesome-single-cell
description: Community-curated list of software packages, data resources, researchers, and publications for single-cell analysis.
longDescription: seandavi/awesome-single-cell is the community-curated canon for single-cell genomics: software packages and data resources for RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and related assays, plus researcher and publication indexes. It is cited in peer-reviewed surveys of the scRNA-seq tool landscape (Zappia et al. 2021, which analyzed 1000+ tools). Still the first link shared with newcomers to single-cell analysis.

name: awesome-small-molecule-ml
description: Curated papers, datasets, frameworks, and packages for machine learning on small-molecule drug discovery.
longDescription: benb111/awesome-small-molecule-ml collects the machine-learning side of small-molecule drug discovery: papers, datasets, frameworks, packages, and blogs. It is a standard reference for ML chemistry benchmarks and data sources. Complements the broader drug-discovery lists with a tighter machine-learning focus.

name: AwesomeGenomics
description: Broad Institute's curated list of genomics resources: databases, software, libraries, toolboxes, pipelines, books, courses, and tutorials.
longDescription: broadinstitute/AwesomeGenomics is the Broad Institute's awesome list for genomics, spanning bioinformatics databases, software, libraries, toolboxes, pipelines, and learning material. Institutional maintenance gives it unusually good coverage of production-grade genomics infrastructure. A genomics-focused counterpart to Awesome-Bioinformatics.

name: BAIO — AI × Biology Briefing
description: Twice-weekly briefing tracking AI x biology news, research, deals, and tools, with a browsable public archive of past issues.
longDescription: BAIO is a newsletter-first intelligence source covering the intersection of AI and biology: models, papers, deals, and tooling distilled into 5-minute reads, delivered twice a week. Its public archive doubles as a searchable timeline of the AI-bio field. Useful for keeping up with new BioAI tools between deeper dives.

name: Benchling
description: Biology-first cloud platform for biotech R&D: structured scientific data, molecular biology workflows, registry and inventory management.
longDescription: Benchling is the de facto lab-informatics backbone for hundreds of biotechs, structuring experiments, sequences and samples in one system. Scientists design experiments, capture structured data and run AI agents and models on top of it. Startup and academic tiers make it ubiquitous across the biotech ecosystem.

name: BindingDB
description: Public web-accessible database of experimentally measured protein-small molecule binding affinities, collecting data since 2000.
longDescription: BindingDB, launched in 2000 as the first public molecular recognition database, holds experimentally measured binding affinities between proteins and small molecules, chiefly drug targets. Its 2025 NAR paper describes it as a FAIR knowledgebase of protein-small molecule binding data, with full dataset downloads hosted via UC San Diego. It is a key supplement to ChEMBL for affinity-prediction benchmarks.

name: bio.tools
description: Community registry of computational tools and data resources for the life sciences, curated under the ELIXIR infrastructure.
longDescription: bio.tools is the long-running community registry of bioinformatics software and data services, maintained within ELIXIR. Entries carry structured metadata (topics, operations, input/output types), making the catalog machine-readable and increasingly relevant for AI agents that need reliable tool discovery. One of the most complete catalogs of life-science software available.

name: BioAI Agents Directory
description: Curated directory of 238+ AI agents and platforms for drug discovery, protein design, clinical trials, genomics, and biopharma R&D.
longDescription: BioAI Agents Directory catalogs 237+ AI agents and platforms transforming biopharma, browsable by category and use case across the R&D value chain. It includes expert comparison guides, category rankings such as protein design platforms, and a submission portal for new tools. A good first stop for surveying the commercial BioAI agent landscape.

name: BioContextAI MCP Server Registry
description: Community registry and open-source collection of MCP servers wrapping STRING, Open Targets, Reactome, UniProt, and Human Protein Atlas.
longDescription: BioContextAI is a community registry that connects agentic AI with biomedical resources via MCP; its proof-of-concept Knowledgebase server federates access to STRING, Open Targets, Reactome, UniProt, Human Protein Atlas, and PanglaoDb. The project is described in a bioRxiv preprint and includes a template and registry editor for submitting new servers. The closest thing to an app store for biology MCP servers.

name: BioGPT
description: Microsoft's domain-specific generative transformer for biomedical text mining and generation, pretrained on millions of PubMed abstracts.
longDescription: BioGPT applied the GPT recipe to large-scale biomedical literature and led biomedical relation-extraction benchmarks like BC5CDR at release. The MIT-licensed repo ships pretrained base and large checkpoints, also available on Hugging Face. It remains a common reference point for domain-specific biomedical language models.

name: Bioinformatics Specialization (UCSD)
description: Seven-course UC San Diego specialization teaching bioinformatics algorithms, from finding hidden messages in DNA to genome sequencing.
longDescription: Created by Pavel Pevzner, Phillip Compeau, and Nikolay Vyahhi at UC San Diego, this Coursera specialization was the first online bioinformatics specialization when launched in 2015 with support from Illumina. Courses progress from Finding Hidden Messages in DNA through Genome Sequencing, gene comparison, molecular evolution, and bioinformatics algorithms. It pairs naturally with the ROSALIND problems and the Compeau/Pevzner textbook.

name: BioMCP
description: Biomedical MCP server and CLI unifying PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and MyVariant.info queries for AI agents in one interface.
longDescription: BioMCP by GenomOncology is an open-source Python MCP server announced as a Model Context Protocol for biomedical AI assistants and agents. One query reaches literature, clinical trial, and genomic variant sources that normally sit behind separate APIs and identifiers; it ships as both a Python package (biomcp-python) and a single-binary CLI. An enterprise extension, OncoMCP, adds HIPAA-compliant precision-oncology deployment.

name: Biomni
description: Open-source general-purpose biomedical AI agent from Stanford that autonomously executes research tasks using 150+ tools and 59 databases.
longDescription: Biomni is Stanford SNAP Lab's general-purpose biomedical AI agent, published in Science in 2025, built to autonomously execute research tasks across diverse biomedical subfields. It integrates LLM-powered agents with 150 specialized tools, 59 databases, and 105 software packages, and is also exposed via Amazon Bedrock integrations. It is currently the most complete open-source foundation for agentic biomedical data work.

name: Biostar Handbook
description: Practical e-book series by Istvan Albert teaching reproducible bioinformatics data analysis, from Unix scripting to RNA-seq and SNP calling.
longDescription: The Biostar Handbook by Istvan Albert is a beginner-friendly, practical e-book series (now five volumes) covering Unix command-line skills, RNA-seq, genome analysis, SNP calling, and more. It is closely tied to the Biostars Q&A community and emphasizes turning large sequencing datasets into reproducible findings. NCI training modules for beginners are built directly on it.

name: Biotech Today
description: Scientific intelligence platform for AI in drug discovery, tracking ~90 AI tools across structure prediction, docking, antibody design, and ADMET.
longDescription: Operated by Avanthus Sàrl, Biotech Today blends editorial deep dives on AI in drug discovery with tool intelligence: benchmarks, maturity scores, and adoption data across categories like protein structure prediction, de novo design, molecular docking, antibody design, and ADMET. It also publishes tool comparisons such as AlphaFold2 vs Boltz-1 vs Chai-1. Part directory, part analyst brief for the TechBio tooling landscape.

name: Boltz
description: Open-source biomolecular interaction models; Boltz-2 adds binding-affinity prediction to AlphaFold 3-level structure prediction.
longDescription: Boltz-1 (2024) was the first fully open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3 accuracy for biomolecular complexes. Boltz-2 (2025) jointly predicts structure and binding affinity, with affinity calculations far faster than physics-based methods, enabling virtual screening. Code and weights are available on GitHub with documentation for local and service deployment.

name: Broad Single Cell Portal
description: Free, open-access Broad Institute portal hosting more than 1,000 single-cell genomics studies with interactive visualization and downloads.
longDescription: The Broad Institute's Single Cell Portal is an open-access, web-based platform for sharing and exploring single-cell genomics data, currently listing over 1,000 studies. It offers interactive visualization, exploratory differential expression, and public downloads, and hosts a curated Human Cell Atlas main collection. It is a key public home for large single-cell atlas datasets alongside CELLxGENE.

name: Chai-1
description: Open-weight model from Chai Discovery for predicting protein, ligand and nucleic-acid complex structures, Apache-2.0 licensed.
longDescription: Chai-1 shipped runnable weights and code that matched AlphaFold 3-class performance on many complex-prediction benchmarks. The chai-lab repo is Apache-2.0 licensed and pairs with Chai Discovery's commercial computer-aided molecular design suite used by Novartis, Pfizer and others. Newer antibody-design models have since been announced on the company site.

name: ChEMBL
description: Manually curated EMBL-EBI database of bioactive drug-like molecules that integrates chemical, bioactivity, and genomic data.
longDescription: ChEMBL is a manually curated, open, FAIR-compliant database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties maintained by EMBL-EBI. ChEMBL 35 contains data on roughly 17,500 approved drugs plus millions of bioactivity measurements linking compounds to targets. It is a Global Core Biodata Resource and the backbone dataset for ML in drug discovery.

name: Claude Code
description: Anthropic's agentic terminal coding tool with filesystem-based Agent Skills; the reference runtime for SKILL.md bio skill libraries.
longDescription: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic CLI for coding and automation, and the flagship consumer of the Agent Skills format: folders with a SKILL.md that teach the agent specialized procedures. Skills are filesystem-based and managed separately from claude.ai/API skills, and Anthropic ships a dedicated life-sciences marketplace on top of it. Most bioinformatics skill libraries in this hub are written to run here first.

name: ClawBio
description: The first bioinformatics-native AI agent skill library: standalone SKILL.md pipeline skills with executable scripts, demo data, and tests.
longDescription: ClawBio packages real bioinformatics workflows — genomics, GWAS, phylogenetics, proteomics, pharmacogenomics, single-cell — as runnable agent skills, each with a SKILL.md contract, executable Python script, demo data, and tests. It is built on OpenClaw/open-agent conventions, local-first and privacy-focused, and every skill also runs standalone via clawbio.run_skill(). The skill count has grown quickly, from 8 at launch to dozens (up to ~96 in recent snapshots) with a growing contributor base.

name: Codex CLI
description: OpenAI's open-source coding agent with experimental Agent Skills support, documented in the openai/codex repo and OpenAI API docs.
longDescription: Codex is OpenAI's CLI/cloud coding agent; its repo openai/codex documents SKILL.md-based skills (rolled out as experimental support) alongside AGENTS.md conventions for steering agents. The official OpenAI docs guide covers packaging instructions, resources, and optional scripts as skills that extend ChatGPT and Codex. A second target runtime for the same cross-compatible skill files used in the Claude ecosystem.

name: ColabFold
description: Free Colab notebooks and local installer pairing AlphaFold2 with fast MMseqs2 alignments, making structure prediction accessible to all.
longDescription: ColabFold brought AlphaFold 2 to every lab by combining it with fast MMseqs2 sequence alignments inside a browser notebook. Published in Nature Methods, it is cited by thousands of structure-prediction studies. LocalColabFold extends the same pipeline to local machines across operating systems.

name: Cradle
description: Web-based AI protein engineering platform that generates and optimizes candidates for stability, activity and expression from your data.
longDescription: Cradle's SaaS lets protein engineers train on their own experimental data so the AI suggests better candidates in fewer experiments. It reports adoption by six of the top 25 pharma companies following a $73M Series B. The ML stack runs on Google Cloud with the open-source Flyte workflow orchestrator.

name: CZ CELLxGENE Discover
description: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative platform to find, download, and visually explore curated and standardized single-cell biology datasets.
longDescription: CZ CELLxGENE Discover (NAR 2025) lets researchers find, download, and visually explore curated and standardized single-cell datasets, with an Explorer for interactive analysis of individual datasets. CELLxGENE Census provides API-based access to the full corpus for large-scale computation, and the underlying Explorer software is open source. It has become a primary hub for cross-tissue single-cell data and models.

name: Deep Learning for the Life Sciences (O'Reilly)
description: O'Reilly book by the DeepChem team on applying deep learning to genomics, chemistry, microscopy, and drug discovery problems.
longDescription: Written by Bharath Ramsundar, Peter Eastman, Patrick Walters, and Vijay Pande (O'Reilly, 2019), this practical book teaches developers and scientists to apply deep learning to genomics, chemistry, biophysics, microscopy, and drug discovery. It is built around the DeepChem library, with runnable examples for molecular property prediction and protein tasks. It remains the canonical bridge between ML engineering and life-science data.

name: DeepChem
description: Python library democratizing deep learning for drug discovery, quantum chemistry, materials science, and the wider life sciences.
longDescription: DeepChem aims to provide a high-quality open-source toolchain that democratizes deep learning in drug discovery, materials science, quantum chemistry, and the life sciences. It offers model implementations, featurizers, and the MoleculeNet datasets, with extensive tutorials collectively known as The DeepChem Book. Its MIT-licensed ecosystem supports both academic research and commercial use.

name: DiffDock
description: MIT diffusion generative model that recasts molecular docking as generation over non-Euclidean manifolds to predict ligand binding poses.
longDescription: DiffDock (arXiv 2210.01776, MIT) frames molecular docking as a generative modeling problem over non-Euclidean manifolds, pairing a score model with a confidence model. It significantly improved blind docking accuracy and speed over classical methods, and is available as an NVIDIA build model card and interactive Hugging Face demo. It became the reference AI docking method that newer generative docking approaches benchmark against.

name: EMBL-EBI Training
description: Free on-demand and live EMBL-EBI training courses covering bioinformatics resources and data-driven life sciences skills.
longDescription: EMBL-EBI Training delivers free, world-class training in data-driven life sciences through on-demand online courses, live virtual training, and in-person courses at Hinxton. Materials cover the major EMBL-EBI resources (UniProt, ChEMBL, and more) and are openly reusable. It is the authoritative way to learn the public bio-data infrastructure underpinning most AI-bio pipelines.

name: ENCODE Project
description: NHGRI program building a comprehensive map of functional elements in the human and mouse genomes, served through a rich data portal.
longDescription: ENCODE (encyclopedia of DNA elements), launched in 2003 by NHGRI, aims to build a comprehensive parts list of functional elements in the human and mouse genomes. Its portal provides thousands of datasets including ChIP-seq matrices, body maps, and single-cell experiments. ENCODE regulatory annotations are core training data for genomic deep-learning models.

name: Enformer
description: DeepMind's transformer that predicts gene expression and chromatin tracks from ~200kb DNA sequences using long-range context.
longDescription: Enformer was the first sequence model to integrate enhancer effects tens of kilobases away from promoters when predicting gene expression. It remains a workhorse for scoring regulatory effects of genetic variants. Its successor AlphaGenome (2025) extends the idea to one-million-base inputs and many more regulatory modalities.

name: ESM-2 / ESMFold
description: Meta FAIR's protein language model family plus ESMFold, predicting atomic 3D structures from single sequences without alignments.
longDescription: ESM-2 scaled protein language modeling to 15B parameters, and ESMFold used it to fold sequences dramatically faster than AlphaFold2. The Science 2023 paper made structure prediction from raw sequence practical on modest hardware. The repo was archived in 2024 as the team spun out to EvolutionaryScale; the active esm package now lives at Biohub/esm.

name: ESM-3
description: 98B-parameter generative protein language model that reasons jointly over sequence, structure and function to design proteins beyond nature.
longDescription: ESM-3 was trained on 2.8 billion protein sequences and generated a novel fluorescent protein unlike anything in nature, published in Science in 2025. It was the debut model of EvolutionaryScale, the startup spun out of Meta FAIR's protein team. Access runs through the company's Forge platform and API, with a smaller open-weight variant available.

name: Evo 2
description: Genomic foundation model trained on 9 trillion DNA base pairs from 100k+ species for genome-scale prediction, interpretation and design.
longDescription: Evo 2 from the Arc Institute models DNA at single-nucleotide resolution across all domains of life, and is now published in Nature. It predicts pathogenicity of human genetic variants and generates functional genome-scale sequences. Code is open on GitHub, weights are on Hugging Face, and the Evo Designer tool exposes design workflows.

name: Galaxy Project
description: Open-source, web-based platform for data-intensive biomedical research letting anyone run thousands of analysis tools without writing code.
longDescription: Galaxy is an open-source, community-driven, web-based platform for accessible, reproducible, and transparent computational research (NAR 2024 platform paper). Its public servers expose thousands of interoperable third-party analysis tools through a point-and-click interface, requiring no user-supplied code. It is one of the longest-running and most widely used platforms in biomedical data analysis.

name: GATK (Genome Analysis Toolkit)
description: Broad Institute's open-source industry-standard toolkit for SNP and indel variant discovery in germline DNA and RNA-seq data.
longDescription: The Genome Analysis Toolkit from the Broad Institute is the industry standard for identifying SNPs and indels in germline DNA and RNA-seq data. GATK 4 is a collection of command-line tools for analyzing high-throughput sequencing data, focused on variant discovery, and is fully open source. Its Best Practices pipelines anchor most production genomics variant-calling workflows worldwide.

name: Gemini CLI
description: Google's open-source terminal AI agent that added Agent Skills, hooks, and TOML-frontmatter custom commands from v0.26.
longDescription: Gemini CLI is an open-source AI agent that brings Gemini models into the terminal, with custom slash commands defined as Markdown files in .gemini/commands. Since v0.26.0 it supports Agent Skills that package specialized expertise, procedural workflows, and task-specific resources, mirroring the SKILL.md ecosystem. Another runtime where community bio skill packs can be installed.

name: Geneformer
description: Foundation transformer pretrained on ~30 million single-cell transcriptomes for context-aware gene-network prediction and transfer learning.
longDescription: Geneformer (Nature 2023, Theodoris et al., Broad Institute) ranks genes by network importance within a specific cell context using only expression data. It enables transfer learning for cell-type classification and in silico perturbation prediction from limited data. Weights and code ship via Hugging Face with documentation on Read the Docs.

name: GeneGPT
description: Tool-augmented LLM from NCBI that learns to call NCBI Web APIs, beating biomedical LLMs on the GeneTuring benchmark.
longDescription: GeneGPT (NCBI, published in Bioinformatics 2024) teaches an LLM to use NCBI Web APIs by in-context learning, answering biomedical questions about genes, diseases, and sequences. It outperformed biomedical LLMs like BioGPT on the GeneTuring benchmark by augmenting the model with domain tools. It is an early, influential demonstration of tool-augmented agents for genomics data access.

name: Generate:Biomedicines
description: Flagship-founded generative biology company programming novel protein therapeutics; published the Chroma protein generator in Nature.
longDescription: Generate:Biomedicines trains generative models like Chroma to create therapeutic proteins beyond what evolution produced. Its platform spans target to molecule with integrated wet-lab validation, plus a multi-target Novartis collaboration. The company positions itself as a drug generation rather than drug discovery company.

name: gget MCP
description: MCP server implementing the gget bioinformatics toolbox, giving agents a standard interface to query genomic databases.
longDescription: gget-mcp, from the longevity-genie organization, wraps gget — the popular command-line tool for querying genomic databases — as a Model Context Protocol server. AI assistants gain structured access to gene, sequence, and annotation lookups that would otherwise require shell commands. It is regularly cited in curated life-science MCP lists such as awesome-genomic-skills.

name: Google DeepMind Science Skills
description: Google DeepMind's official skill pack to speed up agentic scientific workflows with better grounding and token efficiency.
longDescription: science-skills is Google DeepMind's public collection of agent skills for scientific research, spanning genomics and life sciences alongside chemistry, materials, and physics. It was released to make agentic scientific workflows faster and more grounded, and is one of the most-starred science skill repositories (~2.7k stars per tracking lists). A direct way to give any SKILL.md-compatible agent domain competence.

name: GPTomics bioSkills
description: A set of SKILL.md files giving AI agents expert knowledge and code patterns for standard bioinformatics workflows.
longDescription: GPTomics/bioSkills provides AI agents with expert knowledge for bioinformatics work: each skill bundles code patterns and best practices as SKILL.md instructions. It is one of the earlier community attempts to codify bioinformatics practice for coding agents, and appears alongside ClawBio in curated genomic-skill lists. Good raw material for building lab-specific skill sets.

name: GTEx Portal
description: NIH Common Fund resource for tissue-specific gene expression and genetic regulation, with eQTLs across 50+ tissues from ~1,000 donors.
longDescription: The Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) Portal is a comprehensive public resource for studying tissue- and cell-specific gene expression and genetic regulation across roughly 1,000 donors and 50+ tissue types. It provides bulk and single-cell RNA-seq together with eQTL analyses that link genetic variants to expression changes. GTEx eQTLs are a standard ingredient in functional genomics and AI target-prioritization pipelines.

name: Human Cell Atlas Data Portal
description: Global consortium creating comprehensive reference maps of every human cell type, publishing open multi-omic data on millions of cells.
longDescription: The Human Cell Atlas, founded in 2016 as an open global initiative, aims to create comprehensive reference maps of all human cells as a basis for understanding health and disease. Its Data Portal distributes community-generated, multi-omic open data for over 12 million cells with standardized analyses. HCA atlases are the reference against which new single-cell models and AI annotation tools are built.

name: Insilico Medicine
description: Clinical-stage AI drug discovery company running target-to-clinic pipelines on its Pharma.AI suite (PandaOmics, Chemistry42, Medicine42).
longDescription: Insilico's Pharma.AI spans biology (PandaOmics target discovery), chemistry (Chemistry42 generative molecular design) and clinical medicine (Medicine42 trial analytics). Its AI-designed antifibrotic candidate progressing through clinical trials is a landmark for generative-AI drug discovery. The company publishes pipeline and validation details openly.

name: Isomorphic Labs
description: Alphabet spin-out rebuilding drug discovery around frontier AI models, scaled by a $2.1B raise and major pharma partnerships.
longDescription: Isomorphic Labs was created from DeepMind in 2021 to reimagine drug discovery with an AI-first approach. Its AI drug design engine builds on foundation models across disease areas and partners with large pharmaceutical companies. A $2.1 billion funding round is scaling its engine and pipeline globally.

name: MCP Reference Servers
description: Official Model Context Protocol repository of reference server implementations and links to community-built MCP servers.
longDescription: modelcontextprotocol/servers is the canonical collection of MCP reference implementations plus an index of community servers, maintained by the MCP project (Anthropic and partners). It defines the server patterns that bioinformatics MCP servers follow, from filesystem access to database querying. Any agent hub for biology ultimately plugs into this ecosystem.

name: MCPmed
description: Collection of MCP servers for seamless integration with biological and biomedical databases, maintained by the MCPmed org.
longDescription: MCPmed is a GitHub organization publishing a comprehensive set of Model Context Protocol servers for biological and biomedical databases. The collection lets Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients query core life-science resources directly instead of through ad-hoc scripts. Its servers are frequently cross-listed in life-science MCP registries such as BioContextAI.

name: MoleculeNet
description: Classic benchmark suite of 17 molecular machine learning datasets spanning quantum mechanics, physical chemistry, biophysics, and physiology.
longDescription: MoleculeNet (arXiv 1703.00564; published with over 700,000 curated compounds) organizes 17 datasets into quantum mechanics, physical chemistry, biophysics, and physiology categories. All datasets load directly as DeepChem dc.data.Dataset objects, making it the long-standing standard for comparing molecular ML models. Benchmarks like Tox21, ESOL, and HIV from this suite remain ubiquitous in papers and tutorials.

name: MoLeR
description: Microsoft's graph-based molecular generative model supporting scaffold-constrained generation for lead optimization.
longDescription: MoLeR generates molecular graphs directly and can keep a supplied scaffold fixed, so chemists explore decorations around a known lead. The microsoft/molecule-generation repo implements it in PyTorch. It is exposed for conditional small-molecule generation through model services such as OpenAD.

name: NCI Genomic Data Commons (TCGA)
description: NCI's Genomic Data Commons harmonizing and distributing cancer genomics data, including the complete TCGA cohort of 50,000+ cases.
longDescription: The NCI Genomic Data Commons is a next-generation cancer knowledge network providing a repository and computational platform spanning 50,571 cases from TCGA, HCMI, and other programs. It applies uniform harmonization pipelines to genomic, clinical, and biospecimen data (Nature Communications 2021), distributed through the GDC Data Portal. It is the canonical access point for large-scale cancer ML and precision-medicine research.

name: Nextflow
description: Domain-specific language and engine for building scalable, reproducible scientific workflows that portably run on any computing platform.
longDescription: Nextflow enables scalable, reproducible, and portable scientific workflows for research and production, using a domain-specific language on top of a powerful execution engine. Workflows run unchanged across local machines, HPC clusters, and the cloud, which has made it a de facto standard in bioinformatics. The nf-core ecosystem and official training at training.nextflow.io extend its reach.

name: nf-core
description: Community-maintained collection of 156 peer-reviewed, standardized bioinformatics pipelines built on Nextflow, with shared modules and training.
longDescription: nf-core is a community-driven collection of 156 bioinformatics pipelines written in Nextflow, each peer-reviewed and standardized with shared modules and subworkflows. Its 2025 paper in a PMC-indexed journal documents how the framework empowers bioinformatics communities with reusable, best-practice pipelines. Running nf-core pipelines on virtually any computing environment makes production-grade reproducibility practical.

name: Nucleotide Transformer
description: Family of DNA language models up to 2.5B parameters pretrained on 3,200+ human genomes and 850 species for genomics prediction tasks.
longDescription: The InstaDeep Nucleotide Transformer family pretrains BERT-style models on whole genomes and was published in Nature Methods in 2024. Weights are open on Hugging Face and integrate with its transformers library. It is a standard baseline for DNA-language-model benchmarking across regulatory genomics tasks.

name: NVIDIA BioNeMo
description: NVIDIA's platform for AI-driven biology and drug discovery: open models, libraries, datasets and deployable NIM microservices.
longDescription: BioNeMo packages domain models for protein structure, molecular generation and genomics as customizable NIM microservices and cloud services. It lets biotech and pharma teams build and scale generative-AI drug-discovery pipelines on NVIDIA GPUs. Partners use it for workflows from target discovery to virtual screening.

name: OpenClaw
description: Open-source AI agent framework that runs on your devices and chat channels, with a SKILL.md-based skill system and the ClawHub registry.
longDescription: OpenClaw is a free and open-source autonomous AI agent gateway (TypeScript, MIT) that connects LLMs to tools and messaging channels like Discord, iMessage, and Teams. Skills are defined by SKILL.md files and install from ClawHub, Git repos, or local directories, with gating, allowlists, and environment injection configured per workspace. It is the ecosystem several bioinformatics skill libraries, such as ClawBio, target first.

name: OpenFold
description: Trainable, memory-efficient PyTorch reimplementation of AlphaFold 2, including the complete training pipeline and training data.
longDescription: Unlike the original release, OpenFold lets researchers retrain and modify the model, yielding new insights into how AlphaFold 2 learns and generalizes. It is the backbone of many production and community structure-prediction deployments. The same lab now develops OpenFold-3, a bitwise reproduction of AlphaFold 3.

name: Papyrus Dataset
description: Large-scale curated bioactivity dataset of about 60 million data points assembled from ChEMBL and other sources for ML drug discovery.
longDescription: Papyrus (Journal of Cheminformatics 2023) aggregates around 60 million small-molecule bioactivity data points from ChEMBL, ExCAPE-DB, and smaller high-quality sets, with protein quality categories and consistent structure normalization. The dataset is openly hosted on Zenodo, and the Papyrus-scripts library provides programmatic access for ML and proteochemometrics modeling. It is widely used for training and benchmarking bioactivity prediction models.

name: ProteinMPNN
description: Baker lab's graph neural network for inverse folding, designing amino-acid sequences that fold into a target protein backbone.
longDescription: ProteinMPNN is the standard companion to structure generators like RFdiffusion, rewriting backbones into sequences that fold correctly. The Science 2022 method outperformed physics-based design in silico and experimentally, and handles multimer design. Successors LigandMPNN and NA-MPNN extend it to ligands and nucleic acids.
publisher: Baker Laboratory (UW Institute of Protein Design)

name: PyMOL
description: User-sponsored molecular visualization system on an open-source foundation, maintained and distributed by Schrödinger.
longDescription: PyMOL, created by Warren DeLano and now maintained by Schrödinger, is a comprehensive tool for rendering and animating 3D molecular structures. It ships with an open-source foundation on GitHub plus free educational builds and commercial incentive versions, with the current release being PyMOL 3.1. Its scriptability has made it a long-standing favorite for publication-quality molecular figures.

name: RCSB Protein Data Bank
description: US host of the worldwide Protein Data Bank, providing experimentally determined 3D structures of proteins and nucleic acids with analysis tools.
longDescription: RCSB PDB (rcsb.org) curates and annotates data from the single worldwide archive of experimentally determined 3D structures of large biological macromolecules. It offers powerful search, an interactive Mol* 3D viewer, and educational resources via PDB-101, described in its NAR database issue paper. Nearly every protein AI model, from AlphaFold to diffusion designers, is trained or evaluated against PDB structures.

name: RDKit
description: Open-source cheminformatics toolkit with a C++ core and Python wrappers for 2D/3D molecular operations and ML descriptor generation.
longDescription: RDKit is a collection of cheminformatics and machine-learning software written in C++ with Python wrappers, distributed under a business-friendly BSD license. It handles 2D and 3D molecular operations, substructure search, and descriptor generation for machine learning on Mac, Windows, and Linux. It is the foundational library underlying most open-source cheminformatics stacks.

name: Recursion
description: TechBio company industrializing drug discovery with the Recursion OS platform, robotic wet labs and massive multimodal biological datasets.
longDescription: Recursion maps cellular phenotypes at massive scale by pairing automated experiments with multimodal AI. The Recursion OS platform spans target identification through clinical-trial enrollment, and its merger with Exscientia consolidated two of the largest AI-drug-discovery organizations. Its research engine Valence Labs advances the underlying ML.

name: RFdiffusion
description: Diffusion-based generative model for de novo protein design, including binders, motif scaffolding and symmetric assemblies.
longDescription: RFdiffusion is the de facto tool for generating new proteins from scratch or around functional motifs. Its 2023 release powered a wave of experimentally validated designed binders and scaffolds. RFdiffusion 2 and 3 (2025) extend generation to de novo biopolymers and small-molecule-binding proteins.

name: ROSALIND
description: Platform for learning bioinformatics through automatically graded coding problems, from Python basics to genome assembly algorithms.
longDescription: ROSALIND is a platform for learning bioinformatics through problem solving, effectively Project Euler for biology. Problems are organized into tracks like Python Village, the Bioinformatics Textbook Track, and algorithmic sections, with automated grading of submitted answers. It is the standard way beginners turn biology knowledge into working code.

name: Rosetta Documentation
description: Official documentation and tutorials for the Rosetta macromolecular modeling suite covering structure prediction, docking, and protein design.
longDescription: The official RosettaCommons documentation covers Rosetta's capabilities for structure prediction, design, and remodeling of proteins and nucleic acids, developed since 1998. It includes a Getting Started guide, tutorials, demos, and protocol captures for protein design and protein-protein docking, complemented by the Leman et al. 2020 Nature Methods paper. Rosetta remains the classical, physics-based counterpoint to modern deep-learning protein design.

name: RoseTTAFold
description: Baker lab's three-track neural network for accurate protein structure and protein-complex prediction, part of the Rosetta ecosystem.
longDescription: RoseTTAFold was one of the two celebrated 2021 methods that solved single-chain structure prediction, running in minutes on a single GPU. Its All-Atom successor extends prediction to assemblies containing nucleic acids, ligands and covalent modifications. It remains a foundation of the Rosetta protein-design software ecosystem.

name: Scanpy
description: Scalable Python toolkit for single-cell gene expression analysis, covering preprocessing, clustering, trajectory, and visualization.
longDescription: Scanpy (scverse ecosystem) is a scalable Python toolkit for analyzing single-cell gene expression data, built jointly with the anndata format. It provides the standard Python workflow for preprocessing, visualization, clustering, trajectory inference, and differential expression. Together with Seurat it forms the two dominant ecosystems for single-cell analysis.

name: scFoundation
description: BioMap's ~100M-parameter single-cell model trained on 50M+ human transcriptomes, modeling ~19,264 genes at full context.
longDescription: scFoundation is built on the xTrimoGene architecture and trained on over 50 million human single-cell transcriptomic profiles. It captures scale-free gene-network structure and powers tasks like cell typing and drug-response prediction. Weights are mirrored on Hugging Face and it is routinely benchmarked against scGPT and Geneformer.

name: scGPT
description: Generative pretrained transformer for single-cell multi-omics, pretrained on 33 million cells for cell typing, integration and perturbation.
longDescription: scGPT was among the first single-cell foundation models built by generative pretraining across 33 million cells. It supports cell annotation, multi-omic integration, batch correction and gene-network inference, with extensive tutorials in the repo. It is a standard baseline in single-cell foundation-model benchmarks.

name: Schrödinger
description: Physics-based computational platform with industry-standard molecular modeling and simulation software for drug discovery and materials.
longDescription: Schrödinger's platform combines physics-based simulation with machine learning to advance small-molecule and biologics programs. Its software is used across pharma for computational chemistry, from hit finding to drug formulation. The company also runs its own internal drug-discovery pipeline.

name: SciAgents
description: MIT multi-agent system combining ontological knowledge graphs with LLM agents to autonomously generate and validate scientific hypotheses.
longDescription: SciAgents (Buehler Lab, MIT LAMM; arXiv 2409.05556, published in Advanced Materials) automates scientific discovery by coupling large-scale ontological knowledge graphs with multi-agent LLM reasoning. It autonomously generates, critiques, and refines research hypotheses, demonstrated on materials and biomaterials discovery. It showcases how knowledge-graph grounding improves agent-driven hypothesis generation.

name: Seurat
description: R toolkit from the Satija Lab for quality control, analysis, and interactive exploration of single-cell RNA-seq data.
longDescription: Seurat is the R-based single-cell RNA-seq analysis toolkit from the Satija Lab and the counterpart of Scanpy in the Python world. It supports QC, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and cell-type annotation, with an extensive set of vignettes that double as tutorials. A peer-reviewed comparison notes both packages offer wide analysis options and active communities.

name: STRING
description: Database of scored, integrated protein-protein interactions covering 12,535 organisms, 59.3 million proteins, and 20+ billion interactions.
longDescription: STRING (string-db.org, maintained within the SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics) collects, scores, and integrates physical and functional protein associations from experiments, curated databases, and computational predictions. Version 12.5 covers 12,535 organisms and over 20 billion interactions, with confidence-scored downloads and an API. Its networks are standard inputs for graph-based ML and target-discovery pipelines.

name: Tempus
description: AI-enabled precision medicine company with the world's largest clinical and molecular data library, genomic testing and Tempus OS.
longDescription: Tempus connects real-world clinical and molecular data to power oncology decision support, genomic testing and biopharma research. Tempus OS packages that data infrastructure with generative AI at scale for providers and researchers. The publicly traded company collaborates with academic medical centers to accelerate research and patient care.

name: Therapeutics Data Commons
description: Platform of AI-ready datasets, ML tasks, and public leaderboards spanning the full therapeutics pipeline from targets to clinical outcomes.
longDescription: Therapeutics Data Commons (NeurIPS 2021 Datasets & Benchmarks; Nature Communications) is the first unifying platform to systematically access and evaluate machine learning across the entire therapeutics pipeline. Every dataset ships with a defined ML task, train/validation/test splits, evaluation metrics, and public leaderboards, plus reference implementations. It is maintained by Harvard's Zitnik Lab and also distributes datasets via Hugging Face.

name: UCSF ChimeraX
description: UCSF's next-generation interactive molecular visualization program for analyzing structures, density maps, and molecular trajectories.
longDescription: ChimeraX is the next-generation molecular visualization program from UCSF's Resource for Biocomputing, Visualization, and Informatics, succeeding UCSF Chimera. It interactively visualizes and analyzes molecular structures, density maps, and trajectories, and is highly extensible for structure building and analysis workflows. It is free for academic use and standard equipment in structural biology labs.

name: UniProt
description: The world's most comprehensive, freely accessible resource for protein sequences and functional annotation, curated since 2002.
longDescription: UniProt is the world's leading high-quality, comprehensive, and freely accessible resource for protein sequence and functional information, documented in its 2025 NAR paper. The UniProtKB knowledgebase combines expertly curated Swiss-Prot entries with automatically annotated TrEMBL entries, plus BLAST and proteome services. It is the canonical source of protein function data feeding models and knowledge graphs across biomedicine.

name: UW Institute for Protein Design
description: Hub for de novo protein design research, software, and publications from Nobel laureate David Baker's Institute for Protein Design at UW.
longDescription: The UW Institute for Protein Design (ipd.uw.edu) is the home of computational protein design pioneered by 2024 Chemistry Nobel laureate David Baker. Its site publishes research across deep learning, enzymes, peptides, minibinders, and drug delivery, and links to its core labs (Baker, Bhardwaj, DiMaio, King) and their software and AI tools. Following IPD publications is the fastest way to track the frontier of AI protein design.

name: Valence Labs
description: Recursion's AI research engine building virtual-cell, molecular ML and LLM-orchestrated workflow tools for drug discovery.
longDescription: Valence Labs began as Valence Discovery and became Recursion's machine-learning research engine after the 2023 acquisition. It builds virtual-cell models for rapid hypothesis loops and low-data molecular ML methods. Its LOWE project is an LLM-orchestrated workflow engine that hands state-of-the-art AI tools to every discovery scientist.

name: Virtual Lab
description: Stanford framework where a team of LLM AI scientists led by a PI agent collaborates with a human researcher to plan and run scientific projects.
longDescription: The Virtual Lab (Zou Group, Stanford) is an AI-human collaboration in which an LLM principal investigator agent guides AI scientists with different backgrounds who hold their own group meetings. Its flagship result was the design of nanobody binders for SARS-CoV-2 variants, covered by Stanford Medicine and CZ Biohub in 2025. It is a reference architecture for multi-agent virtual research labs.

name: ZINC Database
description: Free multi-billion-scale database of commercially available compounds for virtual screening, spanning 54.9 billion molecules in 2D.
longDescription: ZINC, from the Shoichet Lab at UCSF, is a free database of commercially available ('tangible') compounds for virtual screening; ZINC-22 enumerates roughly 37-55 billion molecules in 2D with billions built in 3D. It is browsed through the Cartblanche interface and powers large-scale docking campaigns with DOCK. Any ligand-discovery agent or virtual screening pipeline ultimately draws candidate compounds from ZINC.
